// Code that must NOT be reported.
//
// The other half of the fixture pair, and the more important one: a check that
// reports everything is as useless as one that reports nothing, and it is the version
// that gets disabled rather than fixed.
package fixture

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os/exec"
)

// An argv array with a validated identifier. The normal, correct shape: argv carries
// no shell, so there is nothing to inject into.
func argvArray(slug string) {
	exec.Command("useradd", "--create-home", "--shell", "/usr/sbin/nologin", slug)
}

// A variable holding a validated value is not "formatting". Flagging this would put
// an annotation on every exec call in the agent, and annotations nobody reads are
// worse than none.
func variableArgument(unit string) {
	exec.Command("systemctl", "reload", unit)
}

// Fixed arguments, whatever they contain.
func fixedArguments() {
	exec.Command("systemd-analyze", "verify", "/etc/systemd/system/rl-web.service")
}

// The word bash appears here, in prose, explaining that bash must never be invoked.
// The scanner walks expressions and never visits comments, so this cannot trip it.
// The TypeScript side learned that four separate times before RL-M1-041.
func prosePlainlyMentionsShAndBashAndZsh() {
	exec.Command("true")
}

// Annotated with a reason, which is what the annotation is for.
func annotatedWithAReason(port int64) {
	//ratline:allow-formatted-arg the port is an int64 validated against the catalogue's bounds, not text
	exec.Command("some-runtime", fmt.Sprintf("--port=%d", port))
}

// A trailing annotation, for a call short enough to read on one line.
func annotatedInline(port int64) {
	exec.Command("some-runtime", fmt.Sprintf("--port=%d", port)) //ratline:allow-formatted-arg bounded int64
}

// THE CASE RL-M2-033 EXISTS FOR: a reason that wraps onto a second comment line.
//
// The check permitted the annotation's own line and the one after it, so this call — one
// line further down than the old rule reached — was reported as an unclassified formatted
// argument, with the explanation of why it is safe printed directly above the error. A
// reason is prose, so wrapping is normal rather than exotic, and an annotation that
// silently stops applying when somebody writes a careful sentence is worse than one that
// never worked: it works right up until the reason is worth reading.
func annotatedWithAWrappedReason(port int64) {
	//ratline:allow-formatted-arg the port is an int64 the catalogue has already bounded to
	// 1..65535, so it cannot carry text, and argv carries no shell for it to reach anyway
	exec.Command("some-runtime", fmt.Sprintf("--port=%d", port))
}

// Three lines, so passing is not an accident of the two-line case.
func annotatedWithAReasonOverThreeLines(slug string) {
	//ratline:allow-formatted-arg the slug matched site_slug before reaching here, which is
	// lower case, digits and single hyphens only — no separator, no leading hyphen that
	// could read as a flag, and no dot that could start a traversal
	exec.Command("useradd", "--home=/srv/"+slug)
}

// Not a process launch at all.
func notAnExec(slug string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("sh -c 'useradd %s'", slug)
}

func withContextButClean(ctx context.Context, unit string) {
	exec.CommandContext(ctx, "systemctl", "reload", unit)
}
